review_kind: complete static implementation review with independently verified supplied immutable gate evidence

findings.title: Cancel/replacement does not cancel earlier-version readers, allowing concurrent obsolete jobs
evidence: draft_reader assigns a new dialog id and starts a fresh connections::spawn thread for every request (lines199–210), without cancelling an earlier reader or retaining a running guard.
The active predicate at lines208–209 checks only the RepoTab-wide alive token and elapsed120s; the token remains alive while the tab is open.
Dialog Cancel/Escape closes only self.dialog (src/repo/dialogs/mod.rs:514–515); replacing DraftLoading similarly leaves the shared alive token untouched.
draft_read lines215–216 reject stale answers, but that happens only after old work has completed.

store::list traverses up to200 refs with multiple Git/object queries each and performs retention cleanup; remote/local operations use bounded per-command runners, but all obsolete readers can remain active simultaneously until their120-second overall deadline.
findings.trigger: Open Earlier versions on a slow or large repository, cancel the loading dialog, and open it again repeatedly while keeping the tab open.
findings.actual: Each canceled request continues running metadata queries/retention cleanup; each replacement adds another worker. Cancel stops display only. Per-request deadlines do not bound the number of simultaneous requests.
findings.expected: Closing/replacing a reader invalidates its own cancellation generation/token immediately; stale readers cease further work. A generation-owned running guard or coalescing policy prevents unrestricted overlap.
findings.confirmation: Deterministic source-level state trace; no new runtime/process/recovery experiment was executed under the current Cargo hold.
findings.required_regression: Use synthetic/injected readers and channels first: after Cancel/replacement, assert the old active predicate becomes false while the tab remains alive; assert stale responses cannot replace the new dialog and repeated requests have bounded active workers. No PID enumeration/signaling needed.

positive_evidence: Opt-in repository-local toggle and pre-operation snapshot precede all checkout/rebase-moving operation steps; failures stop the operation before any step runs.
Original raw index/shared-index bytes remain read-only; private cache flattening handles split/sparse/assume-unchanged state and recovery pins original raw bytes.

Saved roots are trees under a worktree-specific hidden ref namespace, preserving separate index/work trees without creating WIP commits. Retention validates recognized versioned roots and uses old-object CAS deletion.

Recovery pins saved ref/object, HEAD/branch, exact raw index/shared cache, ignore-policy membership and current file bytes; native Git apply checks preserve unrelated hunks/index and replace hardlinked files without mutating peers.

Private empty Git config, explicit no-filter hashing, hooks/fsmonitor/signing disablement, no-lazy-fetch, raw recovery attributes, typed relative paths and bounded readers provide concrete isolation boundaries.
Changed links/special files/conflicts/limits fail closed; untracked nested repository contents and ignored untracked files are excluded. Missing promised objects do not silently download.
Practice goes through repository_command; ready Profile worker context is pinned by connections::spawn. SSH/WSL paths route through typed remote requests rather than local filesystem paths.
limits: No independent runtime/Cargo/OS-process/recovery experiment was run because root reserved all compiler slots; supplied gate logs were independently hash-bound and inspected instead.
Real providers, credentials, SSH/WSL hosts, Windows filesystem behavior and concurrent hostile filesystem races were not exercised.
One confirmed lifecycle blocker prevents approval; no additional definite blocker was established in this batch.
